## Discovery & Translational Science

- **NCoA4 ligand limits ferritinophagy to mitigate renal injury** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43036275/)
  - Researchers identified a small-molecule ligand for nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCoA4) that suppresses ferroptosis by blocking ferritinophagy-mediated iron release.
  - The compound significantly reduced cellular iron toxicity and attenuated tissue damage in preclinical models of kidney injury.

- **APOA5-derived signature links cholesterol metabolism to T-cell exhaustion** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43036274/)
  - An APOA5 gene expression signature was found to bridge cholesterol homeostasis with T-cell exhaustion mechanisms in non-small cell lung cancer.
  - The pathway correlates with tumor immune evasion and stratifies clinical responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade in lung adenocarcinoma.

- **ENTPD5 identified as a genetic target for obesity-associated MASLD** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43035253/)
  - A proteome-wide genetic study identified ectonucleoside triphosphate diphosphohydrolase 5 (ENTPD5) as a key candidate target in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
  - Modulation of ENTPD5 directly influences metabolic reprogramming linked to hepatic lipid accumulation in obesity.

- **Pericyte insulin signaling regulates islet vascular density and β-cell proliferation** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.12.765399)
  - Selective knockout of insulin receptors in pancreatic pericytes (PerIRKO) induced circulating hyperinsulinemia and β-cell hyperproliferation in mice.
  - Pericyte insulin loss expanded islet capillary density but impaired ex vivo microvascular function, compromising glucose-stimulated insulin secretion dynamics.

- **Estradiol-driven Treg expansion coordinates gestational intestinal remodeling** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.11.765966)
  - Pregnancy-induced elevated estradiol levels expand intestinal regulatory T (Treg) cells and upregulate IL-10 secretion.
  - Treg-derived IL-10 directly drives intestinal stem cell hyperproliferation, villus elongation, and nutrient absorption during pregnancy, a phenotype abolished by Treg-specific estrogen receptor deletion.

- **AAV9 vector demonstrates target specificity for renal macula densa cells** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.15.766863)
  - Intraperitoneal injection of low-dose AAV9-GFP in neonatal mice targeted kidney macula densa (MD) cells with high efficiency (~85% of GFP⁺ cells were Nos1⁺ MD cells).
  - The platform enabled MD-specific gain- and loss-of-function studies in vivo, including cell-specific knockdown of *Pappa2*.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Biotech]** **Lexeo Therapeutics reports positive interim Phase I/II data for LX2020 in PKP2-ACM** [BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2122301156680724923)
  - Interim data from the Phase I/II HEROIC-PKP2 trial evaluating AAV gene therapy LX2020 demonstrated favorable biological activity in patients with *PKP2*-mutated arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.

- **Venetoclax plus quizartinib triplet shows promise in unfit AML** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43035765/)
  - Results from the Phase I/II VEN-A-QUI trial demonstrate feasibility and anti-leukemic activity of combining venetoclax and quizartinib with low-dose cytarabine or azacitidine in older, treatment-naive unfit acute myeloid leukemia patients.

- **High-avidity BCMA CAR-T achieves clinical response in AL amyloidosis** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43035762/)
  - Early clinical trial results demonstrate complete hematologic responses following administration of a novel high-avidity BCMA-directed CAR-T cell construct in patients with refractory systemic light chain (AL) amyloidosis.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Biotech]** **Helus Pharma’s HLP003 hits primary endpoint in Phase III MDD trial despite safety signals** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/16/helus-psychedelics-depression-phase-3-trial/) | [BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2122299238508085314)
  - Topline results from the pivotal Phase III APPROACH study evaluating HLP003 as adjunctive therapy in major depressive disorder (MDD) showed a -7.6 point placebo-adjusted change on the MADRS total score at Week 6 (p < 0.0001).
  - Despite meeting the primary efficacy endpoint, the study recorded multiple serious adverse events (SAEs), triggering regulatory scrutiny regarding its safety profile.

- **[Biotech]** **CG Oncology immunotherapy reduces bladder cancer recurrence risk by 68%** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/16/bladder-cancer-immunotherapy-reduced-tumor-recurrence-cg-oncology/)
  - Late-stage trial results for CG Oncology's cretostimogene grenadenorepvec in high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) demonstrated a 68% reduction in the risk of tumor recurrence compared to standard care.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Eli Lilly’s SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS confirms tirzepatide efficacy in pediatric obesity** [JAMA](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43035096/)
  - Results from the Phase III SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS clinical trial published in JAMA demonstrated substantial, statistically significant body weight reductions with once-weekly tirzepatide in adolescents with obesity.

- **Once-weekly ribupatide demonstrates weight loss in GEMINI-1 trial** [JAMA](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43035098/)
  - Data from the randomized clinical trial GEMINI-1 showed once-weekly ribupatide induced significant weight reduction in adults in China with overweight or obesity.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Biotech]** **FDA issues Complete Response Letter for Summit Therapeutics’ ivonescimab** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/15/fda-rejects-ivonescimab-lung-cancer-treatment-summit-therapeutics/) | [BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2122286855064559658)
  - The FDA issued a Complete Response Letter (CRL) for the Biologics License Application (BLA) of ivonescimab, a bispecific antibody targeting PD-1 and VEGF co-developed by Summit Therapeutics and Akeso for non-small cell lung cancer.

- **[Biotech]** **Cardiff Oncology receives FDA Fast Track designation for onvansertib in mCRC** [BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2122298823963984253)
  - The FDA granted Fast Track designation to oral PLK1 inhibitor onvansertib for first-line treatment of *RAS*-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer.

- **FDA adopts "Super Intelligence" terminology under Executive Order 14434** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/science-research/fda-and-super-intelligence/fdas-use-super-intelligence-and-si-under-executive-order-14434)
  - In compliance with Executive Order 14434, the FDA announced it will transition to using the terms "Super Intelligence" and "SI" in place of "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" across newly issued public documents and communications starting November 16, 2026.

- **FDA releases draft guidance on hepatic impairment PK and launches Guidance Snapshot pilot** [FDA Guidance Podcast](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/guidances-drugs/guidance-recap-podcast-pharmacokinetics-patients-impaired-hepatic-function-study-design-data) | [FDA Pilot](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/guidances-drugs/guidance-snapshot-pilot)
  - FDA published draft guidance covering study design, pharmacokinetic analysis, and dosing recommendations for patients with impaired liver function.
  - The agency also launched a Guidance Snapshot Pilot program to provide simplified visual overviews of cross-cutting clinical trial modernization guidances.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Big Pharma]** **Eli Lilly acquires Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/lilly-calytrix-bio-acquire-deal-myelofibrosis-essential-thrombocythemiaenial-/874719/) | [BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2122298512138436862)
  - Eli Lilly reached an agreement to acquire Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion in cash, acquiring precision clinical candidates for myeloproliferative neoplasms, including myelofibrosis and essential thrombocythemia.
  - The acquisition marks Lilly’s 15th company buyout announcement this year.

- **[Biotech]** **Seawolf Therapeutics launches with $100 million Series A and $1.2 billion Sanofi partnership** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/seawolf-therapeutics-dna-versant-startup-financing/874465/) | [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/16/versant-lilly-put-100-million-behind-new-startup-aimed-at-solving-one-of-gene-therapys-thorniest-issues/) | [BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2122296388306469061)
  - DNA therapeutics developer Seawolf Therapeutics emerged from stealth with $100 million in Series A funding backed by Versant Ventures, MPM BioImpact, Eli Lilly, and Novartis Venture Fund.
  - The company also disclosed a research and licensing deal with **[Big Pharma]** Sanofi valued at up to $1.2 billion to address targeted delivery hurdles in gene therapy.

- **Sofinnova Partners closes €725 million crossover fund** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/sofinnova-crossover-fund-ii-european-investment/874656/)
  - Sofinnova Partners secured €725 million for Crossover Fund II, aimed at financing late-stage biopharmaceutical ventures across Europe and North America.

- **Atlas Venture annual report details biotech financing recovery and M&A trends** [Atlas Venture](https://lifescivc.com/2026/11/atlas-venture-2026-year-in-review/)
  - Atlas Venture’s 2026 review highlights sustained private capital inflows and a rebound in public debuts, tracking toward ~60 R&D-stage public debuts (including 30–35 traditional IPOs plus reverse mergers) alongside elevated bolt-on acquisition activity.

## Public Health & Policy

- **Target trial emulation confirms 95% real-world efficacy for nirsevimab against RSV hospitalization** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.12.26367940)
  - A real-world target trial emulation of 4,826 infants within the Kaiser Permanente Georgia system demonstrated that Sanofi/AstraZeneca's nirsevimab reduced RSV-related hospitalization risk by 95% (95% CI: 84–98%) and medically attended RSV by 67% (95% CI: 45–80%) through 180 days post-administration.

- **GLP-1 receptor agonist utilization reaches 10% among US adults** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/11/16/glp1-use-covid-19-vaccines-return-on-investment/)
  - Federal survey data indicates approximately 1 in 10 U.S. adults reported using a GLP-1 receptor agonist drug during the preceding 12-month period ending August 2025.

- **US House Democrats coalesce around 'Medicare for More' healthcare platform** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/16/health-news-democrats-settle-on-medicare-for-more-message/)
  - Congressional Democrats have formally aligned around a "Medicare for More" policy strategy aimed at expanding federal health insurance eligibility and access.

- **Childhood lower respiratory infection mortality displays persistent cross-national gaps** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.01.26361942)
  - Analysis of Global Burden of Disease data (1990–2023) across 204 countries showed no global convergence toward top-performing regional episode-fatality ratio frontiers for childhood lower respiratory infections.

**Worth watching:** Detailed safety subgroup readouts from Helus Pharma's Phase III APPROACH trial of HLP003 in MDD to determine if treatment-emergent adverse events pose an obstacle to regulatory submission.

- Biology & Health
    - [Oats impact your Heart through a Misunderstood Fiber](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S-BQXDRugPk) -- Physionic
        - The video analyzes the physiological and cardiovascular impacts of oats and their primary soluble fiber, beta-glucan, citing multiple clinical and nutritional studies.
        - It evaluates established understanding regarding oat fiber against newer scientific findings on how beta-glucan affects lipid levels and heart health.
        - The discussion details the distinctions in metabolic outcomes between isolated beta-glucan supplementation and whole oat consumption.
    - [416 ‒ The science of mitochondria: their role in health, aging, disease, and much more](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nYrLMyUP4S0) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Peter Attia and mitochondrial expert Nav Chandel examine mitochondrial functions beyond ATP production, focusing on ROS signaling, metabolite production, epigenetic regulation, and immune activation via mtDNA/RNA or cytochrome c release.
        - The conversation outlines mitochondrial dysfunction, glycolytic compensation, aging mechanisms, and clinical assessment parameters including VO2 max and mitochondrial efficiency.
        - It analyzes metformin's molecular targets—including complex I inhibition and intestinal accumulation—evaluating its geroprotective potential, limitations in oncology trials, and potential application in inflammation driven by pollution or viral infection.
        - The experts critique touted mitochondrial interventions and supplements, including Urolithin A, berberine, alpha-ketoglutarate, NR/NMN, SS-31, methylene blue, hyperbaric oxygen, and red light therapy's modulation of cytochrome c oxidase.
        - The discussion addresses cancer cell metabolism, disputing the view that Warburg-effect mitochondria are inherently dysfunctional, and advocates for funding foundational metabolic research.
    - [AI Drug Discovery: Who Gets the Money?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/jENOESNq7ng) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Stephanie Davis examines the growing financial and technological interest surrounding AI-driven drug discovery in healthcare and pharma.
        - The video highlights the core strategic debate regarding whether economic value will primarily accrue to frontier AI foundation labs or specialized biotech enterprises.
        - It analyzes how AI adoption is shifting commercial models and value capture dynamics across the digital health and pharmaceutical sectors.
    - [AI Is Not Just Another Hype Cycle](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/rzuh2gPECaE) -- Health2Tech
        - Bret Waters asserts that the current artificial intelligence technological wave represents a structural paradigm shift rather than a transient Silicon Valley hype cycle.
        - The video discusses how foundational advancements in AI capability possess the potential to fundamentally transform industries and existing technology frameworks.
        - It outlines broader implications for future tech innovation trends and widespread economic adaptation.
